title: Departments With At Least One Employee
description:
Report the `name` of every department that has at least one employee, using `EXISTS`.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
hint: EXISTS only cares whether the correlated subquery returns any row at all — SELECT 1 is idiomatic because the actual selected value is never used.
outputExplanation: Engineering, Sales and HR each have at least one employee, so all three departments are returned.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
All departments have at least one employee
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver'),(3,'HR','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ava','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Eve','E',90000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(3,'Hal','E',80000,3,NULL,'2020-01-01');
